findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and ignores the feature flag
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled` from `FlagSqlExpressions`, then returns `false` in both branches. As a result the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle has no effect: SQL expressions are permanently disabled even when the flag is enabled. If permanent disable is intended, the flag lookup is dead code and should be removed; if the flag is supposed to control availability, this is a logic error that makes the toggle ineffective and prevents safely re-enabling the feature through the existing flag.

findings.title: Legacy SQL command path is disabled only via the stub DB, not an explicit gate
findings.body: `NewSQLCommand` (used by `UnmarshalSQLCommand` for the legacy query path) has no explicit SQL-disabled check. It currently fails only because the new `pkg/expr/sql.DB` methods return `not implemented`, which makes `sql.TablesList` error out. If the DB implementation is later restored or replaced, this path will execute SQL without consulting `FlagSqlExpressions` or the new `ExpressionQueryReader` guard, re-enabling the vulnerable feature. The disable should be enforced at command creation or execution rather than relying on the stub error.

findings.title: No regression test for disabled SQL expressions
findings.body: The security gate for `QueryTypeSQL` was added without any test. There is no regression test asserting that a SQL expression query is rejected even when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled, nor that non-SQL expression types still parse. Without such a test, a later change to the guard or the stub DB could silently restore the RCE/LFI-capable SQL expression path.

findings.title: User-facing error incorrectly says SQL expressions are not implemented
findings.body: When a SQL expression is submitted, the new error is `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. The feature was implemented and is being intentionally disabled for security, so this message misrepresents the state and can lead users to believe their Grafana build lacks the feature rather than that SQL expressions are blocked. Return a clear disabled/unsupported message instead.
